fields.name: Guinea-Bissau: Mpox Outbreak - Jul 2026
fields.description:
The Ministry of Public Health declared Guinea-Bissau’s first mpox outbreak on 4 July 2026. By 20 July, three laboratory-confirmed cases had been reported: two in Bissau, including the first confirmed case in Cuntum, and one in Safim in Biombo Region. Twenty-six contacts were under active follow-up and no deaths had been reported. Delays between symptom onset and isolation, together with the absence of clear epidemiological links between the cases, suggested that undetected transmission was occurring. ([UNICEF, 23 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4222891))

By 13 August, six laboratory-confirmed cases had been recorded, including two new cases during epidemiological week 32. Five cases were in the Autonomous Sector of Bissau and one was in Biombo Region, with no deaths reported. Of 46 suspected cases, 23 involved children under 15, including 16 children aged zero to four years. UNICEF supported government-led coordination, community engagement, infection prevention and control, and water, sanitation and hygiene interventions in priority health facilities. A multisectoral UNICEF response plan was developed in alignment with the national 42-day response plan. ([UNICEF, 14 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4225831))

As of 17 August, Guinea-Bissau had reported seven confirmed mpox cases, all among adults. Six were in the Autonomous Sector of Bissau and one was in Biombo Region, while no deaths had been recorded. The confirmed cases did not appear epidemiologically linked, raising concern about unidentified transmission chains amid significant gaps in community surveillance, contact tracing and testing. UNICEF, WHO and other partners continued supporting surveillance, infection prevention and control, water, sanitation and hygiene measures, and public information activities. ([UNICEF, 20 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4226424))

As of 23 August 2026, Guinea-Bissau had recorded 58 suspected mpox cases, including ten laboratory-confirmed cases and no deaths. Around 90% of confirmed cases were in the Autonomous Sector of Bissau, while Biombo Region had reported one case. Suspected cases had also been recorded in Oio, Gabú, Tombali, Cacheu and Bijagós, although there was no evidence of sustained community transmission outside Bissau. Genomic sequencing identified clade IIb, related to viruses circulating in Sierra Leone, Guinea and Nigeria. Of 214 identified contacts, 127 had completed monitoring and 87 remained under active follow-up. WHO classified the outbreak as a protracted Grade 2 emergency and continued supporting surveillance, testing, sequencing, case management, infection prevention, community engagement and cross-border coordination. ([WHO, 27 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230128))

As of 27 September, Guinea-Bissau had reported 23 confirmed mpox cases and 135 suspected cases, with no deaths. Confirmed cases had been recorded in the Autonomous Sector of Bissau, Biombo and Bafata, extending the confirmed geographic spread beyond the areas previously reported. Three confirmed cases involved infants aged 11-12 months. The source of infection was unknown for 74% of confirmed cases, indicating significant gaps in identifying transmission chains. UNICEF continued supporting surveillance, infection prevention and control, water, sanitation and hygiene, and community engagement, while a six-month extension of the response plan was being prepared. ([UNICEF, 7 Oct 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4233098))

fields.name: Bangladesh: Dengue Outbreak - Sep 2026
fields.description:
More than 51,000 dengue cases and 149 deaths were recorded from the beginning of 2026 to 13 September, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). [...] During the first 14 days of September, the country recorded an average of more than 1,200 hospital admissions per day, indicating a continued sharp increase in dengue transmission and the pressure on health facilities. August recorded 20,536 hospital admissions and 43 deaths — more than double the 9,206 admissions recorded in July 2026. [...] The current surge has affected all eight divisions, with Dhaka Division the hardest hit.  ([Bangladesh Red Crescent Society & IFRC, 14 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4229795/))

Bangladesh is experiencing an active and worsening dengue outbreak. By 14 September 2026, 53,570 dengue patients had been hospitalized and 157 deaths recorded, compared with 37,891 admissions and 150 deaths in 2025 [...] The highest burden is currently concentrated in Dhaka, Khulna and Chattogram, while increasing trends have been identified in Pirojpur, Cox’s Bazar and Barguna, with Netrokona also showing an upward trend. The continued increase in cases is placing additional pressure on health facilities, including bed capacity, clinical staff, blood and platelet supplies, and other essential resources. ([IFRC, 23 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4231170/))

fields.name: Liberia: Floods - Aug 2026
fields.description:
Between 19 and 26 August 2026, Liberia experienced a prolonged period of heavy rainfall that affected multiple parts of the country. Initial flooding and localized impacts were reported from 19 August onwards in several communities; however, the situation deteriorated significantly on 24 August 2026, when exceptionally intense rainfall caused widespread overflow of rivers, drainage systems, and waterways, resulting in severe flooding across multiple counties simultaneously.

While seasonal flooding occurs regularly in Liberia during the rainy season, the situation on 24 August represented a clear escalation beyond normal seasonal impacts. The volume and intensity of rainfall exceeded the capacity of existing drainage infrastructure and flood mitigation measures, causing extensive inundation of residential communities, major transportation routes, public facilities, and essential services. The floods rapidly expanded from localized incidents into a large-scale multi-county emergency affecting Montserrado, Grand Cape Mount, Grand Bassa, Bomi, Nimba, River Gee, Bong, and other areas across the country.

The significance of 24 August lies in the fact that this was the point at which the scale of humanitarian consequences exceeded the coping capacity of affected communities and local response mechanisms. Assessments conducted immediately after the flooding confirmed widespread destruction of homes, large-scale displacement, contamination of water sources, disruption of livelihoods, damage to public infrastructure, and growing public health risks. These impacts far exceeded those typically associated with routine seasonal flooding and generated humanitarian needs requiring external support. ([IFRC, 12 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4229812))

The IFRC reported that the floods had affected more than 76,000 people in over 15,200 households and displaced more than 5,000 people. The response targeted 1,225 households, comprising approximately 6,125 people, with assistance including shelter, cash, health, water, sanitation and hygiene support. Of the targeted households, 350 had homes that were destroyed or severely damaged. ([IFRC, 12 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4229812))

fields.name: Cameroon: Cholera Outbreak - Jun 2026
fields.description:
Cameroon's Far North Region is facing a rapidly expanding outbreak. Since late June, more than 1,250 cases and 31 deaths have been reported across nine health districts. The outbreak has already surpassed the scale of recent epidemics recorded in 2019, 2022 and 2024 in Cameroon. Particularly concerning is the situation in Minawao refugee camp, home to over 81,000 refugees, where dozens of cases have been recorded. To bolster the response, $1 million was allocated from CERF to support cholera prevention, treatment, water and sanitation interventions targeting 230,000 people, including children and refugee populations in high-risk border areas. The funding comes as humanitarian partners struggle with severe shortfalls under the country's humanitarian response plan. ([OCHA, 10 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4229293))

As of September 20, 447 cholera cases and four deaths have been reported in Minawao Refugee Camp, which currently is home to more than 81,000 refugees and operating at about 325% of intended capacity. In Cameroon, there have been 2,753 cases and 77 deaths across 11 health districts. ([IMC, 22 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230953))

On 6 October, International Medical Corps reported that the latest government figures recorded 2,903 confirmed cholera cases and 84 deaths across 13 health districts in Cameroon, giving a case fatality rate of 2.89%. As of 5 October, Minawao refugee camp had recorded 459 cases and four deaths. The camp hosted approximately 81,000 refugees and was operating at 325% of its intended capacity, increasing pressure on water, sanitation and health services. International Medical Corps supported a 65-bed cholera treatment centre and had trained 105 health workers to strengthen the response. ([IMC, 6 Oct 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4233070))

fields.name: Niger: Floods - Sep 2026
fields.description:
As of 1 September, floods have affected 34,372 people (5,470 households), causing 44 deaths and 95 injuries. Maradi, Zinder and Dosso are the worst affected, with 4,412 houses collapsed, 43 classrooms damaged, livestock losses and destroyed food stocks. Priorities include household assistance, emergency shelter, protection of displaced people and restoration of essential services. The National Meteorological Directorate forecasts relatively stable conditions, with low likelihood of extreme weather and limited additional flood risk. At the same time last year, floods had affected 92,133 people and caused 50 deaths. ([OCHA, 8 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4228914))

As of 14 September 2026, floods across Niger had affected 57,356 people in 8,214 households, killed 65 people and injured 118. Maradi, Zinder and Dosso were the worst-affected regions. The floods had caused 7,512 houses to collapse, damaged 253 classrooms and resulted in significant losses of livestock and food stocks. ([OCHA, 22 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230946))

fields.name: Philippines: Floods - Aug 2026
fields.description:
The Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) has intensified over the Philippines, bringing persistent and at times heavy to intense rainfall over western and northern Luzon, Metro Manila, and parts of MIMAROPA and the Visayas. The enhanced monsoon is being further influenced by an two LPAs east of Extreme Northern Luzon, which may develop into a tropical cyclone and is expected to continue enhancing the Habagat. As of 29 August 2026, PAGASA has issued multiple heavy rainfall warnings, including Red Warning over parts of Metro Manila and Occidental Mindoro, with serious flooding and landslides possible in affected areas. ([IFRC & Philippine Red Cross, 29 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/philippines/phl-flood-08-2026-phl-enhanced-southwest-monsoon-habagat-2026-08-29))

The latest cumulative National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) Situational Report no. 27 from 30 August reported 7,467,238 people affected, with more than 1,500 areas flooded since the beginning of August. With combined damages to agriculture and infrastructure, the full cost is estimated at over 8 billion pesos (over 100 million CHF). 32 people have died and 17 injured by monsoon-related incidents. [...] According to NDRRMC, a total of 26,197 families (93,636 people) have been displaced, with 43,175 people temporarily taking shelter inside 529 evacuation centres as of 30 August. Almost 66,000 farmers and fisherfolk have been affected, and almost 60,000 hectares of Crops have suffered damages with around 10,000 hectares destroyed. In total the Agricultural sector has suffered estimated damages of over 2 billion pesos. ([IFRC, 2 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4228227))

According NDRRMC report as of 14 September, approximately 9.6 million people (2.8 million families) had been affected, with 44 fatalities, 18 injuries, and 5 people reported missing. Around 157,000 people remained displaced, including 76,000 people temporarily sheltering in 748 evacuation centres. ([AHA Centre, 14 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4229724/))

fields.name: Nepal: Flash Floods - Aug 2026
fields.description:
A major flash flood struck Rasuwa district after a sudden and intense surge of water entered the Bhote Koshi River from the Tibet (China) side at approximately 9:15 AM [on 26 August 2026]. The flood rapidly impacted the Timure, Rasuwagadhi, and Syabrubesi areas, causing significant damage to settlements, markets, police infrastructure, roads, and hydropower facilities. Authorities have warned that rising water levels could affect downstream communities along the Trishuli River corridor. ([IFRC, 26 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227103))

According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), 10,000 households require immediate relief. At least 157 deaths have been confirmed and nearly 245 people remain missing, including security personnel, customs officials, foreign tourists and residents, while search and rescue operations continue. ([WFP, 27 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227331))

Five days after the flash flood of the Trishuli River swept through Raswuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, the Government of Nepal’s response efforts continue at scale, with more than 10,000 people rescued and over 20,000 personnel mobilised for search and rescue operations, while authorities report 903 fatalities and 4,247 people still missing. The Government has officially declared a flood emergency in 15 municipalities and designated two additional municipalities as impacted, underscoring the scale of humanitarian needs across the affected areas. ([OCHA, 31 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227820))

The Rasuwa floods have claimed 1,003 lives, with 3,916 people still out of contact and 11,814 rescued (NDRRMA, 1 September, 13:00). 3,458 displaced people are living in 27 displacement sites in Nuwakot and Rasuwa, mostly in schools. Parts of Tarkeshwar (Nuwakot) have received no assistance, all wards of Aamachhodingmo (Rasuwa) remain inaccessible by road, and four rural municipalities in Dhading lack safe drinking water. Access remains the main constraint. While relief supplies are available, damaged infrastructure, including 41 destroyed bridges and blocked highways, is limiting delivery to remote communities. Following a joint Resident Coordination Office, OCHA, and WFP mission to Nuwakot on 31 August, partners are establishing a coordination hub in Bidur to strengthen operational coordination and address response gaps. ([OCHA, 1 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4228040/))

Alongside the Government of Nepal, the Humanitarian Country Team launched a [Flash Appeal](https://reliefweb.int/node/4228417) in support of the Government-led response. The appeal seeks US$49.6 million to provide life-saving assistance to 84,270 people (19,284 households) in 17 municipalities across six districts: Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan, Gorkha and Tanahu. All identified affected people are targeted, of whom nearly 40 per cent are children. ([OCHA, 3 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4228558))

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reported that, as of 7 September, the floods have claimed 1,356 lives; 4,894 people remain missing and 13,396 people have been rescued. 3,629 displaced people are living in 37 displacement sites in Nuwakot, Rasuwa, Dhading, and Kathmandu. Operations are shifting from search and rescue to relief and recovery, although rescues continue. On 5 September, WFP launched cargo drones to deliver food across difficult last-mile access barriers to flood-isolated communities in Rawuwa. ([OCHA, 8 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4229005))

The humanitarian impact continues to deepen, with widespread displacement, extensive infrastructure damage and significant recovery needs across affected districts. Reported fatalities have risen to 1,403, with 6,150 people missing and 13,742 rescued. More than 2,000 displaced people are staying in 29 holding centers in Dhading, Nuwakot and Rasuwa. The Government's Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment estimates USD 5.3 billion in recovery and reconstruction, with infrastructure accounting for three-quarters of total requirements. Approximately 1.6 million people are affected, 7,570 homes damaged and 783 MW of energy infrastructure has been impacted. ([WFP, 17 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230296/))

Response and recovery efforts continue across flood-affected districts as the Government and humanitarian partners support affected communities while access challenges persist in some areas. Several flood-affected settlements in northern Rasuwa remain inaccessible by road and continue to depend on air-supported humanitarian deliveries. Reported fatalities have risen to 1,453, with 5,644 people still missing and 13,795 rescued, while the floods have caused extensive damage to settlements. Over 1,112 displaced people are staying in 21 holding centers in Dhading, Nuwakot and Rasuwa. ([WFP, 24 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4231270/))

As of 14 September, 2,418 people were staying in 33 government holding centres, including 1,499 people in Nuwakot, 825 in Rasuwa, and 94 in Dhading. The movement of people from holding centres to alternative places like host families or their own abandoned homes continues. As of 21 September, 1,342 people are taking shelter in holding centers across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading districts. ([IFRC, 25 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4231577))

The floods have claimed 1,453 lives; 5,285 people remain missing and 13,795 have been rescued (NDRRMA, 26 September, 19:00). 1,109 people remain in 21 displacement centres in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading. ([OCHA & UN RC Nepal, 29 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4232179/))

As of 4 October, Government authorities reported 1,455 deaths and 5,285 people missing, while 1,085 people remained in 17 holding centres across three districts. Recent heavy rainfall between 24 and 28 September further disrupted response activities and constrained access to affected areas at least by a week. Health services remain disrupted, particularly in Rasuwa, where four health facilities were destroyed and communities served by two facilities continue to face access constraints. Three facilities in Dhading were partially damaged, while 13 health workers remain missing. The Government’s Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment identified 64 damaged water-supply schemes, with estimated losses of approximately US$2.9 million, and sanitation requirements estimated at US$2.6 million. A government-led assessment of 34 schools found that 11 were destroyed and 12 damaged, affecting 9,430 students and 216 teachers. Six schools and one campus continue to host displaced people. Priority needs include learning materials for 4,000 children in Rasuwa, rehabilitation of schools used as shelters, repairs to damaged school WASH facilities. ([UNICEF, 5 Oct 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4232747/))

fields.name: Lao PDR: Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description:
Since late June 2026, Lao PDR had experienced recurrent flooding, flash floods, waterlogging and landslides associated with the southwest monsoon, Tropical Storm Maysak and subsequent weather systems. While flooding was first reported in late June, the situation progressively worsened through July and August as prolonged and repeated heavy rainfall caused cumulative impacts, with already affected areas experiencing further flooding, waterlogging and landslides, increasing damage and disrupting access.

[...] According to the LRC consolidated assessment dated 17 August 2026, flooding during July and August 2026 affected communities across six provinces: Khammouane, Savannakhet, Bolikhamxay, Luang Namtha, Xiengkhouang and Champasak. The assessment covered 25 districts and 395 villages, affecting 22,390 households (114,037 people), including 54,699 women, 13 persons with disabilities and one death. ([IFRC, 25 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227079))

According to the latest Government data, 403,133 people from 81,484 families had been affected across 16 provinces. At least 7,528 people had been evacuated, with eight deaths, three injuries and one person reported missing. The situation continued to shift geographically, with northern provinces among the hardest hit. In Luang Namtha, severe flash flooding on 29 August affected 2,463 households; floodwaters reached the Boten Special Economic Zone, and six temporary shelters were established after the province was declared a disaster zone. Oudomxay experienced its third and most severe flood wave on 29-30 August, which affected 81 villages across Namor, Xay and La districts, while Luang Prabang recorded flash flooding. Khammouane continues to face significant cumulative impacts, with approximately 151,000 people affected across all 10 districts since July. ([UNFPA, 21 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230629/))

fields.name: Honduras: Drought - May 2026
fields.description:
Since May 2026, Honduras has been facing a progressive deterioration in climatic conditions associated with the delay in the start of the rainy season, the irregular distribution of rainfall, high temperatures, and the influence of the El Niño phenomenon.

According to the Center for Atmospheric, Oceanographic and Seismic Studies (CENAOS), during May precipitation deficits of more than 50% were recorded in sectors of the center and south of the country; In June, the impact extended to municipalities in the center and east, with deficits of more than 40%, conditions that persisted during the first half of July. These developments have increased the risk of meteorological drought, potentially affecting water availability, agricultural production and the livelihoods of the most at-risk communities. Faced with this scenario, on August 18, 2026, the Secretary of State in the Offices of Risk Management and National Contingencies (COPECO), through Alert Bulletin No. 028-2026, declared a Red Alert for 75 municipalities due to drought associated with the El Niño phenomenon, located in the departments of Choluteca, Comayagua, El Paraíso, Francisco Morazán, La Paz and Valle; likewise, it declared a Yellow Alert for 71 municipalities and a Green Alert for 88 municipalities. The alerts were issued indefinitely. ([IFRC, 24 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4226903))

fields.name: Sierra Leone: Flash Floods - Aug 2026
fields.description: On the night of 3 August 2026, Freetown experienced approximately six consecutive hours of exceptionally heavy rainfall, triggering widespread flash flooding, severe soil erosion, and multiple slope and structural failures across several densely populated urban and peri-urban communities. [...] Unlike the localized flooding commonly experienced during the rainy season, this event affected 1,763 families (8,915 people), damaged or flooded more than 700 houses, including over 300 houses in Portor Community alone, caused four fatalities, displaced thousands of people, contaminated 18 community boreholes, damaged a community school, and disrupted livelihoods and access to essential services. [...] The crisis has been further compounded by continuous rainfall across Freetown and other parts of Sierra Leone from 4 to 7 August 2026, which has caused additional flooding in other communities and continues to increase pressure on drainage systems, waterways, and unstable slopes. ([IFRC, 18 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4226142/))

fields.name: Indonesia: Earthquake - Aug 2026
fields.description:
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck offshore Nagekeo Regency, East Nusa Tenggara Province, on 15 August 2026 at 04:58 WIB. The earthquake occurred at a depth of 15 km, approximately 38 km northeast of Mbay. The tsunami warning issued for several coastal areas was officially lifted by BMKG at 07:31 WIB. As of 16 August 2026 at 00:00 WIB, BNPB reported 47 fatalities and 101 injuries. More than 5,000 people remain displaced, including 3,356 people in Sikka, 2,078 in Manggarai, and 500 in Nagekeo. Additional displacement was reported in Bima and the Selayar Islands. Preliminary assessments recorded 914 houses severely damaged, 126 moderately damaged, and 317 slightly damaged. At least 93 educational facilities, 36 health facilities, and 38 government offices were also affected. BMKG recorded 341 aftershocks with magnitudes ranging from 2.5 to 6.2. Continuing aftershocks, damaged roads, electricity outages, and communication disruptions are affecting assessments and humanitarian operations. The Larantuka–Maumere road is accessible, while the Ende–Nagekeo road remains cut off. ([IFRC & PMI, 16 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4225800))

The number of IDPs increased to 9,290 people, based on the BNPB update at 00.00 WIB. The details include 3,356 Sikka people—1,356 in the Samador GOR and 2,000 spread independently in 10 points—Manggarai 2,078 people, and Nagekeo 500 people. [...] The earthquake shock was followed by 341 aftershock activities. The number of fatalities recorded to date is 47 people, with the highest death toll in Manggarai Regency with 23 people and East Manggarai with 17 people. Meanwhile, other fatalities were spread across Sikka Regency with 4 people, West Manggarai with 1 person, Ende with 1 person, and Nagekeo with 1 person. At least 101 residents were reported injured with varying degrees of severity. Damage increased significantly compared to previous reports: BNPB now records 914 houses severely damaged, 126 moderately damaged, and 317 lightly damaged—a total of 1,357 houses. The affected facilities include 93 educational facilities, 36 health facilities, and 38 government offices. ([MPBI, 17 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4225822))

As of 18 August 2026, 69 people were reported dead and 1,199 injured, including 115 people with serious injuries and 1,084 with minor injuries. A total of 46,252 people remain displaced, including 46,181 people across the seven affected regencies in East Nusa Tenggara and 71 people in Bima Regency, West Nusa Tenggara. [...] Preliminary damage included 5,713 houses severely damaged, 2,098 moderately damaged and 3,402 slightly damaged. A further 283 educational facilities, 211 health facilities, 97 government buildings, 96 places of worship and 106 business premises or offices were affected. ([IFRC & PMI, 18 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4226044))

according to BNPB, emergency response period for M7.7 Earthquake in East Nusa Tenggara has been extended until 12 September 2026, while response and early recovery operations remain ongoing. Authorities continue to focus on emergency assistance while accelerating rehabilitation and reconstruction planning in affected areas. As of 31 August at 0900H UTC+7, BNPB records 120 fatalities, 1,658 injured persons, and approximately 188,673 displaced persons. ([AHA Centre, 30 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227777))

fields.name: Pakistan: Flash Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description:
The 2026 monsoon season has commenced across Pakistan, with the first spell of seasonal rains affecting several parts of the country and increasing the risk of flash floods, riverine flooding, landslides, and other weather-related hazards, particularly in vulnerable and mountainous areas. [...] Between 28 June and 1 July 2026, monsoon-related incidents were reported in Gilgit-Baltistan and Lower Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. In Diamer District, a flash flood damaged 5–6 houses, washed away one vehicle, and temporarily disrupted road access for around 400 households, while in Ghizer District, rising water levels in River Ghizer caused localized flooding affecting several households. In Lower Chitral, flash flooding damaged residential houses, standing crops, and orchards. ([IFRC & Pakistan Red Crescent, 1 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4218910))

Among the significant incidents reported during the period, a cloudburst on 19 July in Lari Mengal, Doga Top, and Katha Peeran (Union Council Salkhala, Tehsil Athmuqam, District Neelum, AJK) triggered a flash flood that damaged educational institutions, residential houses, commercial shops, and vehicles. Rescue teams and relevant government departments immediately initiated response operations, rapid damage assessments, and the relocation of affected families to safer locations. On the same day, heavy rainfall triggered flash flooding in Rupal Valley, Sub-Division Shounter, District Astore, Gilgit-Baltistan, where no casualties or damage to residential houses were reported, although minor damage to agricultural crops occurred. Subsequently, on 21 July, another flash flood in Louse Village, District Astore, inundated several residential houses, damaging household belongings and essential assets. ([IFRC & Pakistan Red Crescent, 21 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4222382))

Monsoon 2026 has caused 158 deaths and 470 injuries across Pakistan. 1350 houses have been damaged, affecting 585 livestock and 27.84 km of roads. 1,114 rescue operations have been conducted, with 8,714 persons recued or evacuated. 81 relief camps have been established, providing assistance to 804 persons. ([OCHA, 17 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4225950))

Per the National Disaster Management Authority's report, by 21 August the cumulative death toll since 26 June had crossed 163, with more than 483 people injured nationwide. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has recorded the highest number of fatalities, followed by Punjab, Sindh, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Baluchistan. House and roof collapses account for majority of all deaths, followed by flash floods, drowning and lightning strikes. ([IFRC & Pakistan Red Crescent, 23 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4226714/))

fields.name: Colombia: Earthquake - Aug 2026
fields.description:
According to information from the Colombian Geological Service (SGC), an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.4 was recorded on Monday, August 10, 2026, in the morning, with its epicenter in the town of San José del Palmar, in the department of Chocó, located on the Colombian Pacific coast, at a depth of 82 kilometers.

Although the epicenter was in the department of Chocó, direct impacts were also felt in the departments of Caldas, Risaralda, and Valle del Cauca. Preliminary reports from media outlets and municipal governments indicate damage in the capitals and other municipalities of these departments: in Valle de Cauca, 3 people were injured in El Cairo and 2 died in El Zarzal, in addition to the collapse of 20 buildings and minor structural damage to 2 hospitals; in Risaralda, 18 people died; and in Chocó, 10 people were injured and 3 are missing. The number of people affected in the area continues to rise, and the President of the Republic has established a Unified Command Post. ([Cruz Roja Colombiana & IFRC, 10 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4225066))

fields.name: India: Flash Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description: The Assam floods began on 19 July 2026, triggered by exceptionally heavy monsoonal rainfall, which reached up to 490% above normal levels in parts of Upper Assam. Rising river levels and continuous rainfall caused floodwaters to spread rapidly across multiple districts, inundating villages, agricultural land, and critical infrastructure. The situation worsened throughout the following week as flooding expanded, and the number of affected people increased steadily. The emergency reached its peak on 27-28 July, when more than 800 villages were inundated and flood impacts were at their highest. Charaideo, Sivasagar, and Jorhat emerged as some of the worst-affected districts, experiencing widespread village inundation and damage to livelihoods and agriculture. Since late July, receding river levels and improving weather conditions have led to a gradual improvement in the flood situation. However, despite the overall decline in flood impacts, 1,144,733 people remain affected across eight districts, with floodwaters still impacting 437 villages. While the crisis has moved beyond its peak, significant humanitarian and recovery needs persist in the most affected areas. ([IFRC, 6 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4224648))

fields.name: Tajikistan: Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description: On 11 July 2026, at approximately 15:40 local time, following intense rainfall, flash floods and mudflows affected the villages of Darg and Kazdon in Shamtuch Jamoat, Ayni District, Sughd Region. The disaster caused significant damage to residential houses, auxiliary structures, agricultural land, drinking water supply and irrigation systems, electricity infrastructure, internal village roads, and private property. The affected population experienced disruptions to essential services and livelihoods. [...] According to the official assessment, 672 households in the villages of Darg and Kazdon were affected by the flash floods and mudflows. ([IFRC, 24 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4223086))

fields.name: Kyrgyzstan: Flash Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description:
On 13 July 2026, at approximately 19:30 local time, intense short-duration rainfall over the mountainous catchment areas of Nooken district triggered mudflows along two separate channels. The Besh-Korgon channel overflowed and inundated the lower streets of Kochkor-Ata city, destroying 3 electricity poles in the Besh-Korgon settlement. Simultaneously, the Kara-Bulak channel overflowed into Ergesh Aliev village, while separate mudflows descending from higher elevations submerged the villages of Kurulush, Boston, and Kop- Tam in the Mombekov village area. The event occurred in Nooken district, Jalal-Abad oblast, Kyrgyzstan, affecting Kochkor-Ata city and the villages of Ergesh Aliev, Kurulush, Boston, and Kop-Tam.

The mudflows struck the evening of 13 July 2026 (19:30 local time). District civil protection authorities were mobilized the same evening, and clearance and mud-pumping operations were still ongoing as of 02:00 on 14 July 2026. A state of emergency has been declared in the district, and the situation is being monitored by RCSK in coordination with local civil protection authorities. ([IFRC, 24 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4223080))

fields.name: Afghanistan: Flash Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description:
Heavy and continuous rainfall on 20 July triggered flash flooding in several areas of eastern Afghanistan. The impacts have varied significantly between locations with the most severe impacts reported in Parun City, Nuristan Province, alongside flooding in Torkham, Nangarhar Province, and Alingar District, Laghman Province. Parun City was severely affected by a sudden flash flood at approximately 15:00 hrs on 20 July. So far 23 people have been confirmed dead, 15 have been injured with others reported missing. Search and rescue operations are ongoing. ([OCHA, 21 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4222342))

According to preliminary information compiled by the Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS), more than 910 families were affected. The floods caused 31 deaths and 11 injuries, with 77 cases of missing persons reported. Shelter damage was significant, with 910 houses completely and partially damaged, particularly in several provinces of Nuristan, Laghman, Parwan, Logar, Kabul, Kapisa, Panjsher, Nangarhar, Ghazni, Khost ,Maidan Wardak, Paktika and Paktia provinces. In addition, the floods had a severe impact on livelihoods, resulting in the loss of 330 livestock and damage to approximately 5240 jeribs of agricultural land, further increasing vulnerabilities among farming and pastoral households. ([ARCS & IFRC, 25 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4223089))

Beyond Nuristan, flooding and landslides damaged shelter, agricultural land, irrigation systems, education infrastructure and livelihood assets across the affected provinces. Laghman, initially reported as having sustained no residential damage, was confirmed by 28 July to have 187 families affected, 183 houses damaged or destroyed, approximately 800 acres of seasonal crops lost and some 310 livestock lost or damaged. In Paktika, flooding destroyed 14 houses, killed 37 livestock and washed away approximately 122 hectares of agricultural land. Public schools and community-based education facilities were damaged across Nangarhar, Kunar, Nuristan and Laghman. Flooding and landslides may also have displaced or exposed explosive ordnance, creating a secondary hazard for affected communities and responders. ([IFRC, 6 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4224652))

On 3 August, a second flash flood struck Barg-e-Matal district in eastern Nuristan, affecting 191 houses, which were either destroyed or damaged. The floods also damaged bridges, roads, flood protection walls, agricultural land and water supply networks. In the Central Region, flash floods across nine provinces resulted in two fatalities and six injuries. A total of 316 houses were affected, impacting 2,057 people. Approximately 1.6 million square meters of agricultural land were damaged, around 300 livestock were killed, and 17 schools sustained damage, further affecting livelihoods and access to basic services. A separate flooding incident in Paktia province destroyed 11 houses and damaged agricultural land. ([UNICEF, 21 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4226707))

fields.name: Myanmar: Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description:
Heavy and continuous monsoon rainfall caused rising water levels and flooding across low-lying and flood-prone areas of Ayeyarwady Region. The situation escalated on 30 July 2026, when an embankment near Myit Kyo Village in Laymyatna Township breached, and floodwaters rapidly entered Laymyatna town and surrounding communities. The flooding has affected residential areas, agricultural land, roads, and public infrastructure, with communities along the Ngawun River being particularly affected. Water levels in the Ngawun River have exceeded the danger level and remain elevated, with further rainfall potentially worsening the situation. 

The Myanmar Red Cross Society (MRCS) Regional Branch started the response with its own resources on 1 August 2026, and the information indicates impacts across 5 wards, 23 village tracts, and 122 villages in Laymyatna Township; 2 wards, 16 village tracts, and 14 villages in Yegyi Township; and 10 village tracts and 33 villages in Hinthada Township. The most significant impacts are in Laymyethna, Yegyi, and Hinthada Townships, among other townships in Ayeyarwady, particularly communities located along the Ngawun River and other low-lying areas. [...] Approximately 8,907 households, representing 28,455 people, had been affected and displaced to 28 evacuation camps, including community centres, schools, temporary shelters, and monasteries. ([IFRC, 17 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4225954))

In Myanmar, heavy rainfall associated with a Low Pressure Area (INVEST 92W) caused flooding across several townships in Tanintharyi, including Bokepyin, Dawei, Thayetchaung, Launglon, Palaw, and Yebyu. According to DDM, as of 29 Sep, approximately 19K people (1.7K households) were affected, with 2.6K houses and 56 schools affected. Humanitarian assistance has been initiated and continues to be provided to affected communities by the relevant authorities and stakeholders. ([AHA Centre, 5 Oct 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4232604))

fields.name: Chad: Cholera Outbreak - Jun 2026
fields.description:
On 16 June, the Ministry of Public Health and Prevention declared a cholera outbreak in Karal health district, Haraz-al-Biar department (bordering the Lac province and the far-northern Cameroon region), an area hosting more than 30,000 displaced people. Laboratory tests confirmed Vibrio cholerae O1 Ogawa, with 16 cases and one death reported. ([OCHA, 23 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4217493))

As of 23 June, the cholera outbreak in Karal health district, Hadjer Lamis Province, had affected three of the district's 14 health areas. A total of 52 suspected and probable cases, including 9 laboratory-confirmed cases and one death, had been reported. The outbreak remains localized but the risk of further spread is high due to poor water, sanitation and hygiene conditions, the onset of the rainy season, the proximity of the newly affected area to an internally displaced persons site, and shortages of cholera rapid diagnostic tests in the 11 health areas that have not yet reported cases. ([Croix-Rouge du Tchad, 24 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4217808))

As of 29 June, the cholera outbreak in Karal health district had resulted in at least 13 deaths. Health authorities and humanitarian partners continued case management, epidemiological surveillance, household disinfection, community awareness and preparations for an oral cholera vaccination campaign. ([OCHA, 30 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4218619))

By 16 August, the cholera outbreak had spread from Hadjer-Lamis Province to N’Djamena and Lac Province. Laboratory-confirmed cases had been detected in six health districts, while 14 health areas and 65 villages or neighbourhoods had reported at least one case. Nationwide, 484 cases and 21 deaths had been recorded, including 11 community deaths, giving a case fatality rate of 4.3 per cent. Lac Province had become the main area of active transmission, with 218 cases and eight deaths. The Ministry of Public Health and Prevention received 1,924,650 doses of oral cholera vaccine for campaigns in N’Djamena and Lac Province. ([IFRC, 14 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4229793))

As of 7 September, the outbreak had grown to 867 cumulative cases and 42 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 4.8 per cent. Lac Province accounted for 533 cases and 27 deaths, including 96 new cases and 13 deaths reported in Kouloudia during one week. Following an earlier reduction in transmission in Karal, new outbreaks emerged in Massakory and Mani health districts in Hadjer-Lamis Province. Transmission also persisted in several districts of N’Djamena. Oral cholera vaccination coverage exceeded 90 per cent in several targeted districts in Lac Province and N’Djamena, although the response continued to face shortages of safe water, sanitation facilities, medical and WASH supplies, together with difficult access to isolated communities. ([OCHA, 17 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230346))

fields.name: Bangladesh: Flash Floods - Jul 2026
fields.description:
A monsoon depression persisting over south Jharkhand and adjoining Odisha, India, combined with a strong active monsoon current over the North Bay of Bengal, is bringing heavy to very heavy rainfall to Cox's Bazar, Bandarban and Chattogram districts from 6 to 9 July 2026. [...] In the 24 hours to 6:00 AM on 7 July, BMD recorded 283 mm of rainfall in Chattogram, 195 mm in Kutubdia, 129 mm in Cox's Bazar and 128 mm in Bandarban, indicating that the heaviest rainfall band has shifted north into Chattogram while remaining severe across all three districts. 

[...] In the early hours of 6 July, three separate landslides struck Rohingya refugee camps (FDMN) in Ukhiya upazila Jamtoli Camp-15, Kutupalong Camp-7 and Balukhali Camp-11 killing eight people, including five children, when hillsides collapsed onto shelters built on unstable slopes. A ninth person died in a separate landslide in Cox's Bazar municipality. [...] With rainfall intensifying and risk levels rising across all three districts, the cumulative toll has continued to climb: as of 7 July, 10 fatalities and 88 injuries have been recorded across 170 weather-related incidents since 5 July, and the potential for further casualties and damage remains high over the coming days as forecasted. ([Bangladesh Red Crescent, 7 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4220604))

An estimated 1.11 million people have been affected across 10 districts, including more than 12,900 persons with disabilities. As of 12 July, 51 deaths had been reported in connection with the floods and landslides. At least 38,422 people are staying in 1,047 formal evacuation shelters. Flooded roads, damaged bridges, landslides and waterlogging continue to constrain humanitarian access. Preliminary Government reports indicate that 29,741 houses were damaged in Bandarban and Chattogram. ([UN RC Bangladesh, 14 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4221259))

The monsoon depression and subsequent heavy rainfall have created a district-wide humanitarian situation affecting both the Rohingya camps and host communities in Cox's Bazar. As of 12 July 2026, a total of 182,015 affected individuals, 30 fatalities, 39 injured both from camp settlement and host communities in Cox's Bazar from the period of 5-12 July 2026. [...] All 33 camps have been affected by a combination of landslides, flooding, windstorm damage, drowning incidents and infrastructure collapse, resulting in fatalities, injuries, displacement and extensive damage to shelters, WASH facilities, and community infrastructure. As of 12 July 2026, 42,934 individuals have been affected, 9,707 people displaced, 15 deaths, 20 injured reported across the camp settlements. ([IFRC, 18 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4221995))

Heavy monsoon rains, flash floods, and landslides continue to impact communities across Bangladesh, with an estimated 1.28 million people affected in seven districts, including more than 15,500 persons with disabilities. Approximately 436,000 people are estimated to require humanitarian assistance, while 59 deaths have been reported in the seven most affected districts as of 22 July 2026. A total of 74,479 houses have been damaged or destroyed, while flooding has fully or partially damaged 29,076 water points and 36,550 latrines, severely affecting access to safe water and sanitation across 42 upazilas in six districts. [...] Combined losses to the livestock and fisheries sectors are estimated at US$17.3 million across the affected districts. ([UN RC Bangladesh, 23 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4222682))

fields.name: Georgia: Floods - Jun 2026
fields.description:
On 27–29 June 2026, heavy and persistent rainfall struck the Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti, Kakheti Regions in Western Georgia, severely impacting Senaki, Chkhorotsku municipalities and Akhmeta municipality in Eastern over the following days. The continuous rainfall, which began on 27 June at approximately 03:00 AM, led to rising water levels and widespread flooding across multiple communities.

Five villages in Senaki Municipality, (Eki, Zana, Dzvelisopeli, Nosiri, and Teklati), as well as areas of Senaki town, experienced significant flooding. Similarly, in Chkhorotsku Municipality, 13 administrative units [...] were affected. In Akhmeta Municipality, heavy rainfall and flooding accompanied by strong winds affected the 13 communities [...]. Residential houses were damaged, ground floors were flooded, and strong winds caused extensive damage to roofs. Agricultural land and livestock were also affected, resulting in significant livelihood losses for many households.

Local authorities and response teams are currently assessing the situation. As of 29 June, rainfall has subsided in Senaki and Akhmeta, while precipitation continues in parts of Chkhorotsku Municipality. ([IFRC, 7 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4220441))

fields.name: Central African Republic: Cholera Outbreak - Jun 2026
fields.description:
On 26 June 2026, the Ministry of Health and Population declared a cholera outbreak after laboratory confirmation of cases in Bimbo and Mbaïki health districts. As of 1 July, 214 suspected cases and 24 community deaths had been reported, resulting in a case fatality rate of 11.2%. Active transmission had been confirmed in Bangui 2, Bimbo and Mbaïki health districts. The outbreak particularly affected communities along the Ubangi River, where limited access to safe water, sanitation and health services increased the risk of further transmission. ([UNICEF, 6 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/central-african-republic/unicef-central-african-republic-humanitarian-flash-update-no-1-cholera-outbreak-response-6-july-2026))

By 6 July, the outbreak had expanded to 435 suspected cases and 36 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 8.3%. Children under ten years accounted for 44% of reported cases. Transmission continued along the Ubangi River, raising concern about further geographical and cross-border spread. UNICEF supplied cholera treatment kits, oral rehydration supplies and additional tents, increasing the capacity of the national cholera treatment and referral centre from 40 to 70 beds. ([OCHA, 21 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/central-african-republic/west-and-central-africa-latest-events-glance-14-20-july-2026))

By 22 July, 650 suspected cases and 44 deaths had been reported. Cases had spread from Bimbo and Mbaïki to Bangui. The United Nations Central Emergency Response Fund allocated US$1 million to support the response, including disease surveillance, case management, access to safe water and sanitation, community engagement and measures to prevent further transmission. ([OCHA, 22 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/central-african-republic/un-emergency-fund-allocates-us1-million-support-cholera-response-central-african-republic))

In August, UNICEF warned that cross-border transmission, flooding and inadequate water and sanitation continued to increase cholera risks in the Central African Republic. Children under ten accounted for 44% of reported cases. ([UNICEF, 11 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/cholera-spreads-across-borders-west-and-central-africa-unicef-calls-urgent-action-protect-millions-children))

The EU allocated €2.3 million to support cholera responses in the Central African Republic, Cameroon, Chad and Nigeria. ([ECHO, 17 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/nigeria/eu-provides-eur23-million-emergency-humanitarian-funding-curb-cholera-outbreak-west-and-central-africa))

fields.name: Venezuela: Earthquakes - Jun 2026
fields.description:
On 24 June 2026, two strong earthquakes, preliminarily measured at magnitudes 7.1 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, with epicentres near Morón, Carabobo State. The earthquakes were felt across much of the country, including Caracas, La Guaira, Aragua, Carabobo and neighbouring states.  Therefore, the national government of Venezuela declared the state of emergency.

Preliminary information indicates damage to residential and commercial buildings, with reports of structural collapses in parts of Caracas and damage to infrastructure in several affected areas. Search and rescue operations have been activated while authorities continue rapid damage assessments. Power and telecommunications interruptions have been reported in some locations, and hospitals are receiving injured people. ([Cruz Roja Venezolana & IFRC, 25 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4217826))

More than two months after the 24 June earthquakes, the response in Venezuela is increasingly focused on stabilization, while humanitarian and protection needs remain significant. As of August 24, authorities reported 6,509 fatalities, 6,462 people rescued, 226,696 people injured, 60,785 homes evaluated and 25,240 homes damaged, including continued displacement of affected families. Many households remain unable to return home, underscoring the scale of recovery needs ([UNHCR, 16 Sep 2026.](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230180/))

fields.name: Sri Lanka: Dengue Outbreak - May 2026
fields.description:
Dengue cases have been on the rise in the country since the beginning of the year. Following a massive seasonal surge triggered by heavy rains in mid-May 2026, the epidemic trajectory accelerated significantly. Driven by the onset of the southwest monsoon and severe local flooding, the island-wide total quickly advanced from 25,082 cases in early May to more than 35,000 cases by the first week of June, marking an approximate 30% increase compared to the corresponding period of the previous year (as noted by reports via Dengue Visual Atlas).

A higher number of cases is recorded in the Western, Southern, North Western, Sabaragamuwa, and Central provinces, especially in the Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, Kandy, Galle, Matara, and Ratnapura districts. The National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU) reported more than 8,600 new cases of dengue virus within the month of May 2026 alone, raising grave concerns about a potential epidemic. The NDCU also revealed that environmental conditions following high rainfall and major urban flooding are rapidly accelerating the spread of the virus across the country. As of 8 June 2026, a total of nearly 37,000 dengue cases have been recorded across the island, according to data highlighted by NDCU.

Almost 50 per cent of the above-mentioned cases were reported from the Western Province. Indeed, Colombo District recorded the highest number of dengue infections island-wide, accounting for 55.1% of all reported cases nationwide. During week 22, as per the NDCU update, the Colombo District reported a high number of cases (550), followed by Gampaha (531) and Kalutara (265). Outside the Western Province, substantial case numbers were reported from Matara (194), Kandy (173), Ratnapura (160), Galle (142), Hambantota (69), Kurunegala (68), and Kegalle (68), indicating widespread transmission across multiple provinces. ([IFRC, 20 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4217159))

During the 26th week, 6009 suspected dengue cases were reported across all 26 districts, compared to 5238 cases in the previous week, reflecting an 14.7% increase. The Western Province accounted for 56.4% of total cases, with the Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) contributing 2.5%, the rest of Colombo District 17.1%, Gampaha District 29.1%, and Kalutara District 7.7%. Outside the Western Province, notable case contributions were reported from Kandy (8.1%), Matara (6.1%), Galle (4.1%), Kegalle (3.2%) Ratnapura (3.2%), Kurunegala (3.1%), Puttalam (2.8%), and Hambantota (2.4%). ([Govt. of Sri Lanka, 28 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4219647))

During the 28th week, 7633 suspected dengue cases were reported across all 26 districts, compared to 7891 cases in the previous week, reflecting an 3.3% decrease. The Western Province accounted for 53.6% of total cases, with the Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) contributing 3.5%, the rest of Colombo District 17.8%, Gampaha District 24.1%, and Kalutara District 8.1%. ([Govt. of Sri Lanka, 12 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4222025))

During the 30th week, 6014 suspected dengue cases were reported across all 26 districts, compared to 7352 cases in the previous week, reflecting an 18.2% decrease. [...] 137 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas were identified as high-risk, including 8 newly flagged areas. ([Govt. of Sri Lanka, 26 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4223994))

During the 32nd week, 3257 suspected dengue cases were reported across all 26 districts, compared to 4387 cases in the previous week, reflecting an 25.8% decrease. [...] 96 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas were identified as high-risk, including 12 newly flagged areas. ([Govt. of Sri Lanka, 9 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4225962))

During the 34th week, 1802 suspected dengue cases were reported across all 26 districts, compared to 2613 cases in the previous week, reflecting 31% decrease. The Western Province accounted for 52.6% of total cases, with the Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) contributing 3.8%, the rest of Colombo District 20.7%, Gampaha District 20.5%, and Kalutara District 7.5%. Outside the Western Province, notable case contributions were reported from Kandy (10.4%), Galle (5.1%), Kegalle (4.6%), Ratnapura (3.2%), Matara (3.2%), Kurunegala (2.7%), Hambantota (2.4%), Anuradhapura (2.3%), and Badulla (2.3%). ([Govt. of Sri Lanka, 28 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227675))

fields.name: Armenia: Hailstorm - Jun 2026
fields.description:
On 6 June 2026, at approximately 12:56 PM, a severe hailstorm struck the Stepanavan community and surrounding areas in Lori Region, northern Armenia. The hailstorm lasted approximately 15-20 minutes and was accompanied by exceptionally large hailstones, reportedly measuring between 4 and 6 centimetres in diameter. The intensity of the storm caused widespread damage to residential buildings, particularly roofs and windows, leaving many households exposed to weather conditions and subsequent rainfall. Significant damage was also reported to agricultural land, greenhouses, vehicles, public infrastructure, solar energy systems, and livestock.

[...] As of 7 June 2026 (12:30 PM), preliminary assessments conducted by local authorities indicated extensive damage across Stepanavan and Lori Berd communities. In the Lori Berd area, approximately 930 hectares of agricultural land were affected, including 260 hectares in Bovadzor, 350 hectares in Lejan, 250 hectares in Gyulagarak, and 70 hectares in Lori Berd community. Crop losses were estimated to range between 30 and 70 per cent. 

[...] As of 10 June 2026, approximately 1,680 households had been identified as affected in Stepanavan community. [...] In addition, 52 individuals sustained minor injuries, including swelling and soft tissue injuries, although no hospitalizations were reported. Livestock losses included 60 lambs, four ewes, and four foals. ([IFRC, 16 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4216524))

fields.name: Syria: Floods - May 2026
fields.description:
In late May 2026, the Euphrates River experienced severe flooding, expanding to three times its normal size, from 60.9 km² to 188.7 km², following exceptional upstream rainfall and large‑scale dam water releases. The flood inundated 7,210 hectares of agricultural land, equivalent to 8.2% of all cultivated land in Deir‑ez‑Zor Governorate, at a critical time during the wheat harvest period. ([WFP, 3 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4214698/))

Since mid-May 2026, Syria has experienced severe flooding and rapidly rising water levels along the Euphrates River following a sharp increase in water inflow from upstream areas in Türkiye. Affected areas include Deir ez-Zor and Ar-Raqqa governorates in addition to Jarabulus from Aleppo governorate. The increased inflow, reportedly reaching approximately 2,200 m³ per second, is mainly attributed to seasonal snowmelt and the opening of spillways at upstream dams. As reservoir levels exceeded 97% of storage capacity, authorities initiated emergency water management measures, including the opening of three spillway gates at the Euphrates Dam for the first time in more than three decades. The flooding has resulted in the displacement of at least 1,626 families (approx. 8,280 people) in Deir ez-Zor Governorate, partial flooding of displacement sites in Ar-Raqqa, around 30 families, damage to agricultural land and disruption to critical infrastructure, including water stations and local access routes. ([IFRC, 9 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4215560/))

Based on the latest figures from the Directorate of Agriculture (DoA), nearly 20,500 dunumus had been affected by the floods. Oxfam's assessment of 89 farming households across three sub-districts, Al-Tebni, Deir ez-Zor, and Khasham, paints a picture of acute vulnerability. Nearly 85% of the farming population reported total or partial loss of agricultural income. Critically, 85% of irrigation systems (whether individual or community ones) across all surveyed areas are completely nonfunctional due to submerged pump infrastructure and accumulated debris in suction pipes. The flood struck at the worst possible moment, during the harvest season, destroying standing crops of wheat, barley, cotton, and vegetables before they could be collected. Many families have resorted to distress coping strategies: 43% have already sold livestock or productive assets, and a further 25% are planning to take on debt to survive and resume farming. ([Oxfam, 17 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4216671/))

In Aleppo and Idleb governorates, flooding affected more than 19,000 people and damaged over 3,400 shelters, many in displacement sites where living conditions were already fragile. In Al-Hasakeh, flooding displaced more than 1,400 families, with continued impacts reported across urban areas and camps. In Deir-ez-Zor, flooding was particularly significant in Abu Kamal sub-district, where at least 955 households (over 5,600 people) were affected and around 50 families displaced, alongside damage to livelihoods, water systems and infrastructure. Flooding also exacerbated protection risks, including the movement of explosive hazards, increased exposure to unsafe shelter conditions and heightened risks of water contamination and disease. Agricultural losses were reported across affected areas, including damage to approximately 600 hectares of cultivated land, further undermining livelihoods. ([OCHA, 25 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4218420))

The flooding affected an estimated 13,000 households across Ar-Raqqa and Deir-ez-Zor governorates. Approximately 1,753 households were displaced, 859 houses were damaged, and the majority of affected families sought shelter with relatives and host communities, while others were accommodated
in four collective centres. Informal displacement sites and low-lying residential areas were particularly affected, including locations in Ar-Raqqa city and surrounding communities along the Euphrates River in both governorates. [...] Agriculture and livelihoods were among the sectors most heavily affected. More than 30,000 dunums of agricultural land were damaged, while an estimated 120 irrigation pumps were submerged or affected by floodwaters. Local
authorities warned that more than 24,000 hectares of agricultural land remained exposed to flood risks as water levels continued to fluctuate. Poultry farms, irrigation systems and other productive assets were also affected, increasing pressure on farming communities already facing significant economic challenges. ([OCHA, 27 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227375))

fields.name: Philippines: Earthquake and Tsunami - Jun 2026
fields.description:
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck 32 km offshore west of Maasim, Sarangani, at 7:37 a.m. on 08 June. Intensity VIII (very destructive) was reported in General Santos City. A tsunami alert triggered coastal evacuations across nine provinces and was lifted by mid-afternoon. More than 138 aftershocks have been recorded. Initial reports indicate 19 people dead, 12 missing and 134 injured. Figures for affected and displaced people remain provisional pending government validation and ongoing assessments. Homes, government buildings, hospitals and schools have been damaged or destroyed. Power and telecommunications outages have been reported, and damaged roads and bridges are constraining access to some communities. More than 3.2 million learners have been affected. Classes remain suspended in over 6,200 public and private schools pending safety assessments. ([OCHA, 8 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4215278))

According to government authorities, as of 10 June, 45 people have died, 487 have been injured and 17 remain missing. An estimated 197,750 people (43,716 families) have been affected across Regions IX, XI and XII, and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). More than 25,000 people remain displaced, including approximately 16,000 people sheltering in 31 evacuation centres. Widespread damage has been reported, including 7,866 affected houses, of which 1,596 were destroyed, while infrastructure losses are estimated at US$9.2 million. Damage to roads and other critical infrastructure continues to constrain access to some affected and isolated communities. Essential services remain disrupted, including the closure of General Santos International Airport to commercial flights, persistent power outages in several areas and limited access to some municipalities and island communities. ([OCHA, 10 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4215640))

More than 81,100 people remain displaced, with 63,300 people staying with friends or family while the rest (19,700 people) are residing in 46 evacuation centres set up by the Philippines authorities. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) reported that the number of people affected increased to 1.4 million people, with 68 deaths, 1339 injured, and 33 people still missing. Widespread thunderstorms and heavy rainfall across the region compounded earthquake impacts and triggered new landslides, flooded roads and evacuation sites, and contaminated already-damaged water sources. The Government is leading response and recovery efforts and has provided humanitarian assistance worth up to US $3.2 million (PHP 192.4 million) to the affected communities in the form of family food packs and cash assistance. ([OCHA, 18 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4216800))

By 23 June, government figures reported 77 deaths, with about 1.6 million people affected across Regions IX, XI, XII, and BARMM. PHIVOLCS recorded more than 9,400 aftershocks and further seismic activity expected. More than 80,000 houses have been damaged, including nearly 15,000 destroyed, with 884 damaged infrastructure losses and 130 affected roads and 47 bridges limiting access to isolated communities. Eighteen local government units (LGUs) have declared a state of calamity. The Government is leading response efforts, with DSWD assistance exceeding PHP385 million (US$6.3 million), and sectoral agencies working to restore lifeline services. ([OCHA, 23 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4217186))

fields.name: Central/Eastern Africa: Ebola Outbreak - May 2026
fields.description:
On 15 May 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo declared its 17th Ebola disease outbreak after laboratory testing confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease in Ituri Province. Uganda simultaneously confirmed an outbreak following the detection of imported cases from the DRC. On 17 May, WHO determined that the multi-country outbreak constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. As of 21 May, the DRC had reported 746 suspected cases, including 176 deaths, and 83 confirmed cases, including nine deaths. Transmission was concentrated in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces, particularly in Mongbwalu, Rwampara and Bunia health zones. Insecurity, population movements, weak contact follow-up and inadequate isolation and referral systems complicated the response. ([WHO, 21 May 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/disease-outbreak-news-ebola-disease-caused-bundibugyo-virus-democratic-republic-congo-21-may-2026))

The IFRC launched a CHF 29.5 million regional Emergency Appeal in May to support the Red Cross societies of the DRC, Uganda and neighbouring countries. The response focused on community-based surveillance and early detection, safe and dignified burials, infection prevention and control, emergency health services, risk communication, community engagement and preparedness in countries at risk of cross-border transmission. ([IFRC, 3 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/ifrc-scales-ebola-response-drc-critical-supplies-reach-frontline-teams))

On 9 June 2026, the Emergency Relief Coordinator activated the IASC System-Wide Scale-Up Protocol for the Control of Infectious Disease Events in response to the Ebola outbreak in the DRC. The activation was intended to strengthen collective leadership, coordination, operational capacity and accountability as transmission expanded in a context of conflict, displacement and restricted humanitarian access. ([IASC, 10 Jun 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/activation-iasc-system-wide-scale-protocol-control-infectious-disease-events-drc-ebola))

By 29 June 2026, the DRC had reported 1,333 confirmed cases and 399 confirmed deaths. Uganda had recorded 20 confirmed cases and two deaths. Response activities included surveillance and contact tracing, Ebola treatment and isolation facilities, infection prevention and control, safe and dignified burials, laboratory support and community engagement. However, insecurity, population movements, community resistance and inadequate treatment and isolation capacity continued to impede the identification and referral of cases. ([International Medical Corps, 1 Jul 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/ebola-outbreak-drc-and-region-situation-report-9-july-1-2026))

As the outbreak continued to expand, the IFRC revised its Emergency Appeal from CHF 29.5 million to CHF 65 million and increased the target to nine million people. Essential supplies were delivered to frontline teams in Bunia, while the expanded operation sought to strengthen community engagement, surveillance and early detection, safe and dignified burials, infection prevention and control, mental-health and psychosocial support, risk communication, logistics and emergency health interventions. ([IFRC, 3 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/ifrc-scales-ebola-response-drc-critical-supplies-reach-frontline-teams))

As of 12 August 2026, the outbreak had expanded from three health zones in May to 55 health zones, of which 49 had active transmission. More than 4,500 confirmed cases and 2,100 deaths had been reported, with a crude case fatality ratio of approximately 46%. Contact tracing remained incomplete, with only about 20% of cases identified through the follow-up of listed contacts. Health-service use had fallen by more than 40% in some affected areas, while insecurity, displacement and supply-chain disruptions continued to constrain the response. Uganda had reported no new cases since 16 July. ([WHO, 14 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/disease-outbreak-news-ebola-disease-caused-bundibugyo-virus-democratic-republic-congo-uganda-14-august-2026))

On 27 August, WHO and Africa CDC confirmed the end of Uganda’s Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak after 42 days without a new confirmed case following the discharge of its last patient. Uganda recorded 20 confirmed cases, including 15 imported from DR Congo, and two deaths. Surveillance and cross-border preparedness continued because transmission remained active in DR Congo. ([WHO, 27 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4227458))

As of 28 August 2026, the DRC had reported 5,794 confirmed cases, including 2,786 deaths, representing a crude case fatality ratio of 48.1%. At least 1,314 patients had recovered. Cases had been reported across 60 health zones in six provinces, with continuing rapid growth and geographic expansion. ([WHO, 28 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/ebola-disease-caused-bundibugyo-virus-democratic-republic-congo))

WHO determined that the outbreak continued to constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Modelling suggested that the true number of infections could be three to four times higher than reported. WHO called for an immediate and sustained intensification of community-based surveillance, case detection, contact tracing, isolation, clinical care, infection prevention and control, safe burials and community engagement, alongside secure humanitarian access and predictable financing. ([WHO, 28 Aug 2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/second-meeting-ihr-emergency-committee-epidemic-ebola-bundibugyo-virus-disease-democratic-republic-congo-meeting-report-28-august-2026))

As of 16 September 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo had reported 7,258 confirmed Ebola cases and 3,510 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 48.4%. Both confirmed cases and deaths had increased by 9% since epidemiological week 36. The outbreak had expanded to 62 of the country’s 140 health zones across seven provinces—Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo and the newly affected Sud-Ubangi Province. Thirty-five health zones had recorded a confirmed case within the preceding five days, indicating continued intense and geographically expanding transmission. ([OCHA, 16 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230139))

A revised IOM response plan published on 18 September highlighted increased transmission risks associated with displacement and population movements. More than 150 river ports along the Congo River were considered exposed as the outbreak expanded, while approximately 423,000 internally displaced people were living in 54 IOM-managed sites in Ituri and North Kivu and another 1.5 million were living in host communities. Case fatality rates in displacement settings reportedly exceeded 80%, reflecting major gaps in early detection, referral and access to health services. ([IOM, 18 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230408))

On 19 September, MSF and Epicentre launched a vaccination study with the Ministry of Health and other partners to assess whether the ERVEBO vaccine provides protection against Bundibugyo virus. The study will target 20,000 frontline workers in Ituri and North Kivu and include three months of vaccination followed by at least six months of monitoring. ERVEBO was developed for Zaire ebolavirus, although preliminary evidence suggested that it might provide partial protection against Bundibugyo virus. ([MSF, 19 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4230628))

As of 20 September 2026, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo had reached 7,733 confirmed cases and 3,732 deaths. WHO reported 475 additional cases and 222 deaths since its previous weekly report. Dungu Health Zone in Haut-Uélé Province, near the South Sudan border, became the 63rd affected health zone. Ituri remained the main focus, while substantial transmission continued in Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uélé and renewed activity was reported in Tshopo. ([WHO, 24 Sep 2026]\(https://reliefweb.int/node/4231247))

As of 23 September 2026, DR Congo had reported 7,890 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases and 3,799 deaths across 63 health zones in seven provinces. Ituri remained the epicentre, but North Kivu had recorded 567 cases in the preceding 21 days and reached its highest reported incidence in mid-September; its case fatality ratio was 59.7%. WHO reported that 26,980 of 32,342 contacts requiring follow-up had been seen in the preceding 24 hours, or 83.4%. Bulu in Sud Ubangi and Dungu in Haut-Uélé were the most recently affected health zones. ([WHO, 25 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4231511))

On 26 September, Canada announced $36 million to support the Ebola response in DR Congo and surrounding countries. The funding is intended for public health and humanitarian activities, access to care, including for women and girls, and research and development of medical countermeasures. The announcement includes $4 million for medical countermeasure development. ([Govt. Canada, 26 Sep 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4231582))

By early October, North Kivu accounted for nearly 40% of new confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo, compared with 24% at the end of August. Cases were increasing in Beni even as transmission declined slightly in Butembo, and new hotspots continued to emerge. As of 28 September, 34% of confirmed cases were being treated in non-specialized facilities, while more than 60% of deaths occurred in the community. Shortages of beds and specialized treatment capacity continued to hamper isolation and care. ([MSF, 5 Oct 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4232645))

As of 28 September, UNICEF had identified 1,903 children orphaned or separated from their parents because of the Ebola outbreak, including 1,581 in Ituri and 322 in North Kivu, although the actual number was expected to be higher. By 29 September, 2,076 confirmed cases and 1,162 deaths had been recorded among children in cases for which age was known. Around seven in ten infected children under five had died. UNICEF and partners were supporting temporary care, family tracing and reunification, including through 12 nurseries near Ebola treatment centres. ([UNICEF, 6 Oct 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4232805))

On 7 October, WHO reported 8,665 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,178 confirmed deaths in DR Congo. Overall transmission was declining, but new hotspots had emerged near the border with South Sudan, most deaths continued to occur in the community, and contact tracing remained insufficient. Kenya had also notified WHO of a confirmed imported case in a traveller from DR Congo who had transited through Kampala; 55 contacts had been identified, including fellow passengers and crew members. ([WHO, 7 Oct 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4233110))

fields.name: Tanzania: Floods and Landslides - Mar 2026
fields.description:
In late March 2026, prolonged and intense rainfall associated with the March–May rainy season caused severe flooding and landslides in the Mbeya Region, located in Tanzania’s Southern Highlands. The most affected area was Rungwe District, where continuous heavy rains saturated the soil, triggering multiple landslides and flash floods.

The disaster occurred primarily between the evening of 25 March and the early hours of 26 March 2026, with heavy rainfall reported for several consecutive hours. According to local authorities and media reports, the rains were accompanied by strong winds, significantly worsening ground instability and surface runoff.

The worst‐affected wards were Nkunga, Lupepo, Kawetele and Ikuti in Rungwe District. Landslides swept through these communities, burying houses constructed mainly of mud bricks and corrugated iron sheets, while flooding damaged access roads and public infrastructure.

As of 27 March 2026, official reports confirmed that at least 20 people had lost their lives, the majority of whom were children, and several others were injured. Search and rescue operations were ongoing amid continued rainfall, with concerns about secondary landslides and further flooding. ([IFRC, 10 Apr 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4206996))

fields.name: Kenya: Floods - Mar 2026
fields.description:
From 21-22 April, severe thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds battered Mombasa and Kwale counties in south‑east Kenya, triggering localised flooding, displacing residents, damaging homes and disrupting essential infrastructure.
In Mombasa county, media reports dated 22 April indicated that over 100 households were displaced, with extensive damage to dwellings. Flash floods blocked transport routes in Nyali sub‑county, and access to health services was interrupted in Tudor, Mvita sub‑county.
In Kwale county, one person remains missing after being swept away by floodwaters, and five households were affected as well. Additionally, several villages have been cut off and small‑scale farmers face significant agricultural losses.
A further 24‑hour forecast predicts moderate, scattered rain across the south‑east, north‑east and south‑west regions. ([ECHO, 24 April 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4209166))

On 6th March 2026, at approximately 1830 hours, flash floods struck Nairobi and its surrounding areas following an intense six‑hour
downpour. Rainfall levels reached unprecedented highs, with 160 mm recorded at the Wilson Airport meteorological station, 145 mm at
Moi Air Base, 112 mm in Dagoretti, and 117 mm at the Kabete station, all within a span of 3 to 5 hours. The capital city had just
experienced over 534mm of rainfall. The heavy rains swept away bridges, destroyed homes, and rendered major roads impassable, leaving hundreds of residents displaced. The combination of loss of life, widespread property damage, and signicant disruption to critical infrastructure further compounded the crisis. Nationwide, 53 people lost their lives, including 27 fatalities in Nairobi in a single night. ([IFRC, 12 May 2026](https://reliefweb.int/node/4211737))
